A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BiGR and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The original appendix comparisons and image galleries can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet generation and linear-probe results, component ablations, timing measurements, and generated examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds text-to-image outputs, sampling trajectories, and failure examples.

M1.justification: Appendix B adds a text-conditioned variant using T5-XXL embeddings, an additional MLP projection, and text tokens appended to image tokens. This changes conditioning inputs, while retaining the binary tokenizer, masked backbone, Bernoulli transcoder, and sampling procedure.

E1.justification: V2 extends the ImageNet-centered work to text-to-image generation, training on a 20M subset of LAION-400M and the 4M-image JourneyDB. Evaluation examples include short and long natural-language prompts, substantially broadening the represented data and conditioning requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 5 and 9 add SiT-XL/2 with ODE and SDE sampling to the generation comparisons. Existing comparators remain. PixArt, Imagen, and DALL-E 3 supply prompts for the new demonstrations but are not evaluated as text-to-image comparators.

E3.justification: The new text-to-image experiment introduces pretrained initialization and a training schedule specifying 250K, 450K, and 500K steps, changing datasets, resolutions, and batch sizes across phases. It also specifies center-cropping and prompt selection. Existing ImageNet evaluation settings remain unchanged; these are additional protocols.

E4.justification: Appendices C and D add qualitative analyses of how images develop during entropy-ordered sampling and where generation fails, illustrated in Figures 9 and 10. These supplement the retained component and hyperparameter ablations without introducing a systematic robustness benchmark.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. V2 does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial qualitative results for text-to-image generation in Figures 7–8, plus sampling trajectories and failure examples. Tables 5 and 9 add SiT ODE/SDE FIDs of 2.15/2.06 and corresponding metrics. Existing BiGR and comparator scores remain unchanged, so this is expanded evidence rather than a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The binary-code definitions, Bernoulli diffusion formulation, weighted BCE objective, entropy definition, and appendix confidence approximation remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add text-to-image generation as a demonstrated capability. The central claims about unified generation and representation, efficiency, scalability, and the existing zero-shot applications are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of coarse-to-fine sampling and guidance/diversity tradeoffs. It identifies failures involving faces, fingers, text, and complex scenes, attributing them to dataset quality and autoencoder limitations, and qualifies the text-to-image extension by its data, model, training, and resolution limits.

D1.justification: Appendix B provides a substantial new implementation recipe: the T5 checkpoint, 120-token limit, left-padding, projection and conditioning details, preprocessing, initialization, training budgets, and 32 A800 GPUs. However, it inconsistently describes training as 'single stage' before enumerating three stages. Existing configuration tables and code links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for SiT, T5, LAION-400M, JourneyDB, Imagen, and DALL-E 3. Section 4.4 explicitly acknowledges MAR's lowest FID and SiT's leading diffusion results. These update context while preserving the original research positioning; the additional PixArt bibliography entry duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives localized additions and clarifications, including the text-to-image claim and the transcoder explanation. Three new appendix sections precede the retained comparisons, galleries, and ethics statement. Most existing prose and the main section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the visual evidence with prompt-image galleries, an iteration-by-iteration token/image display, and a failure-example panel in Figures 7–10. Tables 5 and 9 gain SiT rows and adjusted layouts. Original image galleries are retained as Figures 11–23 rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence of text-conditioned applicability, makes sampling behavior more understandable, documents concrete failures, and improves comparison coverage with SiT. These strengthen the paper while leaving its central quantitative evidence unchanged. The gain is limited by the qualitative-only text-to-image evaluation and the contradictory single-stage/three-stage training description.
